title: Work Map post-write exact verification dispatch

phases.objective: Bind governed Work Map post-write verification to the exact committed branch head, preserve dispatch stderr, require observable CI and Work Map integration run identities, and align pipeline connectivity governance with the V3 REST dispatch contract.

e2e_journeys.actor: Governed Work Map writer and CI evidence reviewer
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The governed writer completes generation, idempotency proof, commit, push, and branch-head readback.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: CI and Work Map integration are active, accept explicit branch/SHA inputs, check out the committed SHA, and expose verification run IDs whose head SHA equals the writer result head.
steps: Verify the pushed work-branch head still equals result_head_sha.
Read and, when necessary, enable CI and Work Map integration before dispatch.
Dispatch CI through the Actions REST endpoint with expected_head_sha.
Dispatch Work Map integration through the Actions REST endpoint with branch and expected_head_sha.
Persist independent stdout, stderr, and exit-code evidence for both dispatches.
Poll bounded workflow-run listings for workflow_dispatch runs on the target branch whose head_sha equals result_head_sha.
Fail closed unless both dispatches succeed and both numeric verification run IDs are observed.
CI verifies the selected SHA in all load-bearing jobs and binds test/deployment evidence to it.
Work Map integration verifies local checkout identity and current remote work-branch identity.
Pipeline connectivity requires V3 REST dispatch and exact-head run identity signatures while forbidding legacy opaque V2 dispatch signatures.
assertions: The writer does not use opaque gh workflow run calls for post-write verification.
The pipeline connectivity registry requires REST dispatch endpoints, V3 diagnostics, dispatch exit codes, exact-head filtering, and numeric run identity fields.
The pipeline connectivity registry forbids legacy gh workflow run and V2 writer signatures.
Writer-supplied workflow_dispatch inputs are explicitly declared by both receiving workflows.
A disabled verification workflow is enabled and read back as active before dispatch.
Dispatch errors remain available in the writer diagnostic Artifact.
No verification evidence is accepted without an exact matching head SHA and numeric run ID.
Push and pull-request CI execution retain their existing event SHA semantics when no manual expected_head_sha is supplied.
No protected-ref mutation, provider call, deployment, database action, migration Apply, credential payload read, external send, or secret inclusion is introduced.

phases.objective: Publish typed linkage between writer, CI, and Work Map integration run identities across repository evidence families.
Prove exact identity preservation across dispatch retries, concurrent branch movement, delayed run registration, and workflow re-enablement.
This repository CI dispatch correction grants no provider canary authority.
This repository CI dispatch correction grants no Production or deployment authority.
